simple: Animation events are named markers you place at specific moments in an animation, like the exact frame a foot hits the ground. While the animation plays, a script can listen for that marker and do something right then, like play a footstep sound or spawn a dust puff. This keeps sounds and effects perfectly in sync with movement. You can also attach a short text value to each marker to give your script extra info.
analogy: It is like cue marks in a school play script: when the actor reaches the line marked "thunder", the sound crew plays the thunder sound.
keyPoints: The event track is hidden at first. Click the settings icon to the right of the timeline and choose Show Animation Events.
To add one: move the scrubber to the frame, click Edit Animation Events, click + Add Event, type a name, optionally add a Parameter, and click Save.
Once made, an event name can be reused anywhere in the animation, like a `FootStep` marker for both the left and right foot.
Copy a marker with right-click, Copy Selected, then right-click elsewhere and choose Paste Events.
In a LocalScript, use `AnimationTrack:GetMarkerReachedSignal("Name")` and `:Connect` a function to run code when that marker is reached.
The marker's Parameter text is passed to your function, so you can send extra info like `"left"` or `"right"`.

terms.event marker: A small symbol on the timeline that marks when an animation event happens.
terms.parameter: An optional text value saved with the marker, like `"left"`, that your script receives when the marker is hit.
terms.AnimationTrack: A playable copy of an animation loaded onto a character. You call `:Play()` on it and listen to its markers.
terms.Animator: The object inside a `Humanoid` that loads and plays animations.
terms.signal: Something that fires when an event happens. You `:Connect` a function to it to react.
terms.asset ID: The number Roblox gives your published animation, used as `rbxassetid://` plus the number.

example.title: Print which foot stepped
example.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

local player = Players.LocalPlayer
local character = player.Character or player.CharacterAdded:Wait()
local humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid")
local animator = humanoid:WaitForChild("Animator")

-- Point to your published walk animation (replace the ID)
local walkAnim = Instance.new("Animation")
walkAnim.AnimationId = "rbxassetid://5432167890"

-- Load it so we get an AnimationTrack
local walkTrack = animator:LoadAnimation(walkAnim)

-- Run this every time the "FootStep" marker is reached
walkTrack:GetMarkerReachedSignal("FootStep"):Connect(function(paramString)
	print("Step with:", paramString) -- e.g. "left" or "right"
end)

walkTrack:Play()
explain: We find the player's character, its `Humanoid`, and the `Animator` inside it.
We make an `Animation` object and set its `AnimationId` to the published animation's ID.
`LoadAnimation` turns it into an `AnimationTrack` we can play.
`GetMarkerReachedSignal("FootStep")` gives a signal for that marker name; our function runs each time it is reached.
`paramString` is the Parameter text you typed for that marker in the editor.
`walkTrack:Play()` starts the animation so the markers can fire.

watchOut: The marker name in the script must match the editor exactly, including capitals. `"Footstep"` will not catch `FootStep`.
Forgetting to republish the animation after adding events. The game uses the published version.
Not seeing the event track. Turn on Show Animation Events from the timeline settings.
Pasted events land where you right-click, not where the scrubber is.
